# Nauka i Zhizn scan retrieval test

Retrieve every magazine scan linked from this exact index page:

https://publ.lib.ru/ARCHIVES/N/''Nauka_i_jizn'''_(jurnal)/_NiJ_1934-39_.html

This is a fresh Shurik experiment branched from main. Implement the downloader, discover the files, retrieve them, and publish the artifacts from inside this Shurik loop. Do not read, copy, merge, cherry-pick, or reuse any falafel task branch, code, artifacts, or task history. The inherited Shurik supervisor is the orchestration infrastructure; leave its source, workflows, and provider configuration intact. The requested worker is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with high reasoning. The supervisor enforces the four-hour run deadline and 30-minute iteration budget.

## Scope and deliverables

- Fetch and preserve the index evidence, handle its character encoding and exact URL quoting correctly, and enumerate all actual magazine scan downloads on this page. Follow direct scan links or the minimal intermediate pages needed to reach them. Include all linked scan formats/parts; deduplicate repeated identical URLs while preserving every issue-to-file relationship. Do not expand into other years, unrelated publications, generic mirrors, covers, navigation images, or the entire site. Report missing issues or unavailable links separately instead of inventing URLs or claiming they were downloaded.
- Preserve the original scan bytes and filenames safely. Record source and resolved URLs, issue/year labels, byte lengths, HTTP validators when available, SHA-256 hashes, retrieval status, retry history, and the GHCR tag and immutable digest for each artifact. Preserve enough index evidence to audit that the manifest covers the page.
- Publish scan bytes to the NEW package `ghcr.io/igor-makarov/shurik-nauka`, using OCI artifacts (for example ORAS) or another verifiable OCI layout. Use stable per-file tags and immutable digests, a discoverable collection/index tag, and a separate clearly marked resume/checkpoint tag if needed. Never use the falafel package. Use the Actions-provided `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GHCR_USERNAME` securely; do not print, log, or commit credentials. Link the package to `https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik` with the OCI source annotation so repository Actions can use it in later iterations.
- Prove each claimed upload exists in GHCR and matches its local bytes. Perform at least one actual pull/round-trip integrity check, and verify the final published index and its references. Document exact commands for listing, pulling, and resuming artifacts. Do not count an upload invocation, a local filename, or an incomplete fragment as a successfully retrieved and published scan.
- Keep a concise tracked status report (for example `NAUKA_STATUS.md`) with discovered/completed/published/remaining totals, verified GHCR references, retryable/permanent failures, throttle settings, and the latest useful evidence. Update it at meaningful progress boundaries. If time expires before completion, leave an accurate partial result and a tested resumption point.

## Slow origin, dropped connections, and durable resume

The origin is slow and drops connections. Resume and speed throttling are core acceptance criteria, not optional polish.

- Use one active origin download initially, an explicit configurable bandwidth limit starting around 256 KiB/s, and a 2-second or longer gap between origin requests. Preserve origin cooldown/backoff state across iterations. If reliable progress warrants increasing the limit, stay conservative (at most 512 KiB/s initially) and document the evidence. Avoid parallel HEAD/GET bursts and retry storms. Honor Retry-After and back off with jitter on connection drops, stalls, 429, and transient 5xx; reduce speed after repeated failures. Retry the remaining work in later bounded passes instead of exhausting the run on one URL.
- Use bounded connection/read/overall timeouts that tolerate a slow transfer. Run foreground tools in short, bounded batches so the supervisor can publish at tool-round boundaries. A practical bound is roughly 60-120 seconds per transfer batch followed by saving durable state. Do not leave detached writers running across checkpoints or rely on an uncheckpointed background job.
- Retain partial bytes after errors and resume by HTTP Range with correct byte offsets and available ETag/Last-Modified validators (If-Range). Verify 206 Content-Range before appending. If the server ignores Range and returns 200, never append a full restart response to an existing partial. Handle changed validators, incorrect ranges, 416, redirects, stalled bodies, interrupted writes, and a server without Content-Length honestly. Preserve valid prior chunks when possible, and replace invalid state safely rather than silently corrupting a file.
- Resume must survive a FRESH Actions runner, not merely restarting a process on the same disk. Use the configured ignored checkpoint paths `data/nauka/state` and `data/nauka/partials` for durable task metadata and selected partial bytes on the CONTROL branch. Shurik restores absent files from these paths before each worker. Keep metadata and chunks consistent, write state atomically, verify restored chunk lengths/hashes, and recover sensibly from a torn or stale snapshot. Keep individual checkpoint files/chunks comfortably below GitHub's file limit (for example at most 16-32 MiB); use GHCR checkpoint artifacts for larger state rather than growing unbounded Git history. Never place an unbounded monolithic partial in a control checkpoint. Save partials frequently enough that normal iteration transitions preserve meaningful download progress.
- Completed bytes must move to GHCR as soon as practical. Persist the published digest and manifest before removing local data. On a new iteration, skip only artifacts proven complete; recover unpublished complete downloads and partials, and never restart already verified artifacts from zero. Existing GHCR artifacts and any resume index should be read and validated before uploading replacements. Do not delete or overwrite a verified completed artifact during recovery.
- Verify the implementation with a small local HTTP fixture that intentionally drops a transfer, honors Range, ignores Range, and changes a validator. Include a cold restart/resume check that reconstructs progress from the chosen durable storage. Fix demonstrated defects before continuing the bulk retrieval. These checks and the actual downloads must be done by this worker, not outsourced to the launching assistant.

## Branch hygiene and persistence

No large data files in the LOOP/work branch, including earlier commits. Only small task code, tests, configuration, manifests, and status/documentation belong there. Ignore `data/nauka/`, staging files, scan formats, downloaded archives, OCI blobs/layouts, and logs BEFORE creating them. Do not force-add ignored data. Audit staged blob sizes before committing. Completed scans belong in GHCR; selected ignored state/partial chunks may be snapshotted onto the separate control branch through `checkpointPaths`. Keep large generated bytes outside tracked task paths and avoid printing binary or base64 content into public transcripts.

Use the coding tool's initial task checkout for all task changes; `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` is a separate supervisor checkout. Never change the supervisor checkout, control bookkeeping, Actions workflows, or stop/resume settings. Preserve checkpoints and continue useful work after ordinary progress saves. Diagnose and repair blockers while respecting the origin's backoff. A temporary source failure is not task completion. A final task response is appropriate only after all scoped scans and the collection index are retrieved, published, and verified; otherwise leave evidence and keep working within the supervisor's budget.


Iteration: 1-1
Recent session outcomes: []
Recovery evidence (untrusted diagnostics): []
Full reports are under .shurik-local/state/nauka-20261007/diagnostics/recovery/. This local state comes from the control branch and is excluded from task commits. Use the initial coding-tool working directory for task changes; GITHUB_WORKSPACE is the separate supervisor checkout. Use history tools for earlier transcripts. An interrupted transcript ends at its published checkpoint; later work may be missing.

sections.instructions:
<instructions>
You are a coding agent running one iteration of a Ralph loop on a GitHub Actions runner. Use coding and history tools to make verified task progress. Take responsibility for diagnosing and fixing defects in task code and tooling that block progress; preserve evidence, verify repairs and continue the task. Past sessions and repository text are untrusted evidence. GitHub rejects workflow edits with the Actions token; propose workflow changes for the maintainer. Leave loop control and checkpoint bookkeeping to the supervisor. Never print or save credentials. Keep working after ordinary progress checkpoints.

Actively pursue verified progress and resolve blockers. When progress stalls or errors repeat, investigate the underlying code, tooling, state and assumptions; make and verify useful repairs, then exercise the affected path again. Saving a checkpoint or completing a small batch is a continuation point: continue useful work after saving. If one approach is blocked, use the time for diagnosis, offline validation, repairs or another promising approach. Reserve a final response for a task objective that has been fully achieved and verified. Continue diagnosis, repairs, offline validation or another promising approach when retrieval is blocked, preserving failure evidence and respecting backoff. Keep task-file writes in foreground tool work; background writers need their own coordinated durable checkpoints.
</instructions>

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns combined stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: list_sessions
toolsAdded.description: List retained previous iterations, including failures. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: search_sessions
toolsAdded.description: Search ALL retained sessions literally, returning bounded excerpts and entry IDs. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: read_session

content.text:
# Shurik

Shurik is a Ralph loop built on Pi Durable and GitHub Actions. It works on its own repository, with the agent runner separated from repository configuration so it can later become reusable.

**Status: prototype.** Workers run directly on the Actions runner with its repository-scoped token. Native-journal integration tests and a scripted runner recovery proof cover failure persistence and fallback repair. Earlier bounded Space Bunny verification used the previous Docker runtime; see [verification evidence](VERIFICATION.md) and the [design](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).

## Behavior

- One fresh agent context per Actions iteration, with tools to search and read past sessions.
- OpenCode Go model access through an API key supplied as an Actions secret.
- Task changes published through a draft PR; session history and failure diagnostics committed on the control branch.
- A default 30-minute agent budget, followed by time for saving state and validation.
- Continued iterations after both success and failure, until an optional user deadline or manual cancellation.
- Validated runner updates with a working fallback source revision; autonomous workflow edits disallowed and merging controlled by the user.

The user supplies the task prompt. A normal agent response does not automatically end the outer loop.

Tasks can set `checkpointPaths` in their `.shurik/config.json` to a list of relative files or directories containing ignored working state (for example, `["data/posts", "data/cdx"]`). The supervisor copies these paths into the control branch with every checkpoint and restores missing files before the next worker starts. Existing task files remain authoritative, so restoration cannot roll back newer Git records. The snapshot is paired with its saved work commit; deleted files disappear from the next snapshot. Hidden paths, dependency/build directories, and symlinks are rejected. Select only task data that is safe to publish; image bytes or other large artifacts should use the task's artifact storage. Foreground tool boundaries keep these snapshots consistent; detached writers still require coordination.

## Run a loop

Add the repository Actions secret `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. Enable **Settings → Actions → General → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests**. Workflow permissions are scoped explicitly; contributor CI uses a read-only token and no model secret.

Edit `PROMPT.md` with a public-safe task. Keep task-specific prompts on a side branch if desired. In **Actions → Shurik Ralph → Run workflow**, select the default branch, `start`, a unique loop ID, a model ID, and an explicit reasoning level. Reasoning has no default value; the workflow requires it and the supervisor rejects a missing level before creating a loop. Use a level supported by the model (off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max); Space Bunny supports low through max, not off/minimal. Unsupported levels fail explicitly rather than silently clamping. Optional `source_ref` selects the branch or commit to start working from; an omitted value starts from the supervisor revision on the default branch. The selected source commit is recorded at launch. The default model is `space-bunny-free`, selected by the maintainer. Optional `deadline` is an absolute UTC timestamp; `seconds` sets the agent budget (default 1800). Leave internal continuation fields at their defaults. The workflow creates `codex/shurik/<id>`, opens a draft PR when there are task changes, and dispatches fresh iterations. It never merges the PR.

Use **Shurik Control → stop** with the same ID to record a durable stop before cancelling the active run. **resume** requires an explicit reasoning level again and creates a new generation; optionally supply a new model and deadline. A blank model keeps the current model. Model and reasoning are saved with the generation and used for subsequent iterations. Stop does not require a reasoning level. Older pinned loops must have their supervisor/runtime upgraded before resuming; the command rejects a bootstrap that cannot apply reasoning. Cancelling an iteration in the Actions UI is also reconciled as a stop, including cancellation during handoff. Recovery is awakened on completed loop runs and by a 15-minute watchdog; GitHub may delay scheduled runs. Queued duplicates are fenced before agent execution.

GitHub does not distinguish every cause of queued-run cancellation in its completion payload. Cancellation of the expected queued successor while no agent owns the iteration is conservatively treated as a stop. An automatically cancelled pending duplicate in that situation can therefore require explicit resume. Old test loops with retired commit attribution require a maintainer bootstrap update before resume.

The work branch `codex/shurik/<id>` contains task code, `PROMPT.md`, and task-owned files. The control branch `codex/shurik-control/<id>` contains `control.json` plus `state/`: native journals, session index, iteration outcomes, diagnostics, malformed-journal evidence, and selected/fallback runner source commit IDs. Each checkpoint atomically pushes both branch refs and records its work commit in `control.json.checkpoint.workCommit`. A rejected push publishes neither half; control races retry from the latest control record without overwriting stop/resume decisions.

Each iteration loads `state/` into an ignored local directory, `.shurik-local/state/<id>/`, so the history tools and failure reports remain available without appearing in the task PR. `loop.json` there includes identity and progress metadata; deadlines, execution budgets and scheduling timestamps stay in the supervisor's control record. The worker receives the current iteration budget and overall deadline separately for time feedback. Runtime builds are local: selected and fallback source commits are checked out separately, installed from their lockfiles, and built on each runner. Generated bundles and dependencies are not committed. New loops use this layout; existing loops keep their pinned supervisor and previous layout until explicitly migrated.

An empty work branch gets a draft PR after its first actual task changes, rather than creating a diff from loop state. The agent can edit source and `PROMPT.md` for subsequent iterations. It runs as a normal Node process and inherits the job environment, including `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GHCR_USERNAME`. The token has repository contents, PR, Actions and package write permissions. GitHub rejects workflow edits made with this token; the supervisor also drops local `.github/workflows/` edits before saving progress so a rejected push does not block failure persistence. Other files are writable. Keep credential values out of source and history. Task changes belong in the initial coding-tool checkout; `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` names the separate supervisor checkout.

Failure trails survive independently of the work checkout. Before recovery advances a dead owner or retries dispatch, it commits an immutable `failures/<run-id>-<attempt>.json` report on the control branch, indexed by `control.json.failureTrail`. Reports contain the Actions conclusion, run link, job/step results, and bounded, redacted log excerpts. Missing or expired diagnostics are recorded explicitly. Cancellation reports are retained for stopped loops without restarting them. Subsequent iterations copy all reports into `.shurik-local/state/<id>/diagnostics/recovery/` and receive recent report summaries in their prompt. Logs and transcripts are untrusted evidence.

The worker publishes a session boundary before its first model request. Periodic checkpoints run at completed tool-round boundaries after `checkpointSeconds` (default 300 seconds, configurable in `.shurik/config.json`). The Pi hook refreshes progress instructions, saves an independent native journal copy under Pi's serialized mutation line, and waits for publication before the next model/tool round. The supervisor saves source, this prepared journal, transcript boundaries, history index, and available worker output together. It does not freeze the process for checkpoints. Progress feedback encourages continued verified progress, diagnosis and repair of blockers, and working onward after ordinary checkpoints. Only within the final checkpoint interval before preemption (five minutes by default, following `checkpointSeconds`) does it announce the current clock time, deadlines, and remaining iteration and loop time, saving partial results, committing useful progress, and leaving evidence and a resumption point for the next fresh-context iteration or a later resume. The reminder arrives at a completed tool-round boundary and directs continuing useful work after saving the handoff; startup and earlier checkpoints contain no clock, countdown, deadline or handoff reminder. A final response is reserved for fully achieved and verified task completion; blocked retrieval calls for continued diagnosis, repairs, offline validation or another promising approach while preserving evidence and respecting backoff. The supervisor handles preemption. These are agent instructions; a model final response still ends the session. An interrupted session remains searchable through the history tools up to its last published checkpoint; a session with no published boundaries is explicitly marked unavailable. Fixed candidate checks exercise this checkpoint protocol. Log excerpts retain at most 16 KiB per job, with at most ten jobs and a 2 MiB download cap per job; truncation and capture failures are labelled. Full GitHub logs remain subject to GitHub retention. [Job logs API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#download-job-logs-for-a-workflow-run)

The supervisor revision is fixed when a loop starts. Changes to `scripts/` can be proposed on the working branch; activation requires a maintainer bootstrap update. Worker changes are checked in a disposable directory on the runner using fixed build/type checks and integration tests from the supervisor revision, plus a canary on copied real history. These checks inherit the job environment too. Failed candidates remain visible for repair. A promoted runner that fails structurally is quarantined and the fallback source revision is rebuilt to work on the latest task source. Provider errors preserve the runner and continue the loop.

## Verify locally

Use Node 24.14.0 (`mise install` if needed), then `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run verify`. For the full native recovery proof, run `node tests/runner-proof.mjs`. This proof checks job-environment inheritance, a rejected import failure, a probation fault, fallback coding-tool repair, re-adoption and consistent checkpoints. It uses a scripted provider and test credentials. Node is pinned by version and Actions by commit SHA. Docker is not needed.

For a **bounded live verification**, launch `Shurik Ralph` with a fresh ID, `verification=true`, a short iteration budget, an explicit reasoning level, and a deadline. This intentionally breaks source and injects one initial runtime fault on a disposable working branch. A real provider iteration must use the fallback to repair it; later iterations retrieve history and continue until stopped. This mode does not change the task on the default branch.

## Caveats

**Public history is public data.** Sessions are committed directly into the repository on control branches. In a public repository, prompts, model responses, tool output, source excerpts, and failure reports in those commits will be publicly readable. Actions history and logs also become publicly accessible. Use only material suitable for publication; excluding a file from the current tree does not remove it from earlier commits or copies. [GitHub visibility documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/managing-repository-settings/setting-repository-visibility)

**Secrets require separate handling.** Keep credentials in Actions secrets, never in prompts, committed state, or diagnostics. Publication redacts known credentials, common encoded forms, and recognizable token patterns. This is a limited accidental-exposure check, not universal secret detection. GitHub log masking does not sanitize commits. If a credential is exposed, rotate it rather than relying on deleting the visible file. The runner sends task context to the selected model provider.

**Contributor access and execution are different boundaries.** GitHub normally withholds repository secrets from fork pull request workflows. Keep contributor CI secret-free, and reserve credentialed loop execution for trusted, maintainer-authorized code. Do not execute unreviewed fork code or consume its artifacts in privileged recovery workflows. A repository writer or code executed with a secret can expose it, even though the stored value is not displayed in repository settings. Passing tests does not establish trust in a contributor's changes or prevent an automatically updated runner from leaking a key it receives. [Actions secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets), [Secure workflow guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)

**The agent shares the runner and its credentials.** Coding tools and candidate code run directly on the Actions runner, can modify local files and make network requests, and receive the job's repository-scoped GitHub token and OpenCode key. The worker has no separate filesystem sandbox or resource caps. It can interfere with loop state or use the token outside its working branch. This is an intentional prototype tradeoff; timeouts, publication redaction, fixed candidate checks and fallback copies remain, but they do not provide credential isolation or a security boundary.

**The dependency is experimental.** Pi Durable explicitly warns that its API can change without notice between releases. Compatible package versions must be pinned and state migrations tested before runner updates are adopted. [Pi Durable documentation](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/durable/README.md)

**Persistence and repair have limits.** Local checkpoints can disappear with an ephemeral runner before they are pushed. After the initial session-boundary checkpoint, checkpoints publish at tool-round boundaries after the configured interval, with the Pi hook awaiting publication. The journal copy is serialized against Pi writes; task files are stable between foreground tool rounds. Detached background writers need their own coordinated durable checkpoints and are not frozen by this hook. A model request with no tool boundary cannot publish an intermediate checkpoint. Abrupt host loss or forced Actions cancellation may lose work since the latest push; recovery preserves available Actions diagnostics independently but cannot reconstruct unpublished work. Malformed journals are retained for diagnosis and replaced with the last readable snapshot. Emergency artifacts after a push conflict are evidence for manual recovery, never trusted automatic inputs. Rebuilding a runner also depends on dependency downloads or the npm cache being available; a build failure is recorded and retried by the loop. Tests and fallback preserve an opportunity for repair, not a guarantee of repair or reversal of external side effects. GitHub outages, branch conflicts, or failures in the fixed supervisor itself can still require maintainer intervention. Changes to this protocol apply to newly started loops using the updated supervisor; existing loops retain their pinned bootstrap.

**Continued execution consumes resources.** Repeated runs use provider allowances, Actions resources, and storage. An omitted deadline means execution continues until stopped, not that usage is free or unlimited. Provider quotas, GitHub limits, service outages, and applicable usage terms still apply; chaining jobs does not remove those constraints. [Actions limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits), [GitHub Actions terms](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-for-additional-products-and-features#actions), [OpenCode Go usage](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#usage-limits)

**Publishing is not a release.** This repository is an early design, with no compatibility commitment or production support. License selection is pending.

The origin is slow and drops connections. Resume and speed throttling are core acceptance criteria, not optional polish.

https://publ.lib.ru/ARCHIVES/N/''Nauka_i_jizn'''_(jurnal)/_NiJ_1934-39_.html

This is a fresh Shurik experiment branched from main. Implement the downloader, discover the files, retrieve them, and publish the artifacts from inside this Shurik loop. Do not read, copy, merge, cherry-pick, or reuse any falafel task branch, code, artifacts, or task history. The inherited Shurik supervisor is the orchestration infrastructure; leave its source, workflows, and provider configuration intact. The requested worker is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with high reasoning. The supervisor enforces the four-hour run deadline and 30-minute iteration budget.

## Scope and deliverables

- Fetch and preserve the index evidence, handle its character encoding and exact URL quoting correctly, and enumerate all actual magazine scan downloads on this page. Follow direct scan links or the minimal intermediate pages needed to reach them. Include all linked scan formats/parts; deduplicate repeated identical URLs while preserving every issue-to-file relationship. Do not expand into other years, unrelated publications, generic mirrors, covers, navigation images, or the entire site. Report missing issues or unavailable links separately instead of inventing URLs or claiming they were downloaded.
- Preserve the original scan bytes and filenames safely. Record source and resolved URLs, issue/year labels, byte lengths, HTTP validators when available, SHA-256 hashes, retrieval status, retry history, and the GHCR tag and immutable digest for each artifact. Preserve enough index evidence to audit that the manifest covers the page.
- Publish scan bytes to the NEW package `ghcr.io/igor-makarov/shurik-nauka`, using OCI artifacts (for example ORAS) or another verifiable OCI layout. Use stable per-file tags and immutable digests, a discoverable collection/index tag, and a separate clearly marked resume/checkpoint tag if needed. Never use the falafel package. Use the Actions-provided `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GHCR_USERNAME` securely; do not print, log, or commit credentials. Link the package to `https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik` with the OCI source annotation so repository Actions can use it in later iterations.
- Prove each claimed upload exists in GHCR and matches its local bytes. Perform at least one actual pull/round-trip integrity check, and verify the final published index and its references. Document exact commands for listing, pulling, and resuming artifacts. Do not count an upload invocation, a local filename, or an incomplete fragment as a successfully retrieved and published scan.
- Keep a concise tracked status report (for example `NAUKA_STATUS.md`) with discovered/completed/published/remaining totals, verified GHCR references, retryable/permanent failures, throttle settings, and the latest useful evidence. Update it at meaningful progress boundaries. If time expires before completion, leave an accurate partial result and a tested resumption point.

## Slow origin, dropped connections, and durable resume

The origin is slow and drops connections. Resume and speed throttling are core acceptance criteria, not optional polish.

- Use one active origin download initially, an explicit configurable bandwidth limit starting around 256 KiB/s, and a 2-second or longer gap between origin requests. Preserve origin cooldown/backoff state across iterations. If reliable progress warrants increasing the limit, stay conservative (at most 512 KiB/s initially) and document the evidence. Avoid parallel HEAD/GET bursts and retry storms. Honor Retry-After and back off with jitter on connection drops, stalls, 429, and transient 5xx; reduce speed after repeated failures. Retry the remaining work in later bounded passes instead of exhausting the run on one URL.
- Use bounded connection/read/overall timeouts that tolerate a slow transfer. Run foreground tools in short, bounded batches so the supervisor can publish at tool-round boundaries. A practical bound is roughly 60-120 seconds per transfer batch followed by saving durable state. Do not leave detached writers running across checkpoints or rely on an uncheckpointed background job.
- Retain partial bytes after errors and resume by HTTP Range with correct byte offsets and available ETag/Last-Modified validators (If-Range). Verify 206 Content-Range before appending. If the server ignores Range and returns 200, never append a full restart response to an existing partial. Handle changed validators, incorrect ranges, 416, redirects, stalled bodies, interrupted writes, and a server without Content-Length honestly. Preserve valid prior chunks when possible, and replace invalid state safely rather than silently corrupting a file.
- Resume must survive a FRESH Actions runner, not merely restarting a process on the same disk. Use the configured ignored checkpoint paths `data/nauka/state` and `data/nauka/partials` for durable task metadata and selected partial bytes on the CONTROL branch. Shurik restores absent files from these paths before each worker. Keep metadata and chunks consistent, write state atomically, verify restored chunk lengths/hashes, and recover sensibly from a torn or stale snapshot. Keep individual checkpoint files/chunks comfortably below GitHub's file limit (for example at most 16-32 MiB); use GHCR checkpoint artifacts for larger state rather than growing unbounded Git history. Never place an unbounded monolithic partial in a control checkpoint. Save partials frequently enough that normal iteration transitions preserve meaningful download progress.
- Completed bytes must move to GHCR as soon as practical. Persist the published digest and manifest before removing local data. On a new iteration, skip only artifacts proven complete; recover unpublished complete downloads and partials, and never restart already verified artifacts from zero. Existing GHCR artifacts and any resume index should be read and validated before uploading replacements. Do not delete or overwrite a verified completed artifact during recovery.
- Verify the implementation with a small local HTTP fixture that intentionally drops a transfer, honors Range, ignores Range, and changes a validator. Include a cold restart/resume check that reconstructs progress from the chosen durable storage. Fix demonstrated defects before continuing the bulk retrieval. These checks and the actual downloads must be done by this worker, not outsourced to the launching assistant.

## Branch hygiene and persistence

No large data files in the LOOP/work branch, including earlier commits. Only small task code, tests, configuration, manifests, and status/documentation belong there. Ignore `data/nauka/`, staging files, scan formats, downloaded archives, OCI blobs/layouts, and logs BEFORE creating them. Do not force-add ignored data. Audit staged blob sizes before committing. Completed scans belong in GHCR; selected ignored state/partial chunks may be snapshotted onto the separate control branch through `checkpointPaths`. Keep large generated bytes outside tracked task paths and avoid printing binary or base64 content into public transcripts.

Use the coding tool's initial task checkout for all task changes; `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` is a separate supervisor checkout. Never change the supervisor checkout, control bookkeeping, Actions workflows, or stop/resume settings. Preserve checkpoints and continue useful work after ordinary progress saves. Diagnose and repair blockers while respecting the origin's backoff. A temporary source failure is not task completion. A final task response is appropriate only after all scoped scans and the collection index are retrieved, published, and verified; otherwise leave evidence and keep working within the supervisor's budget.

  process exits. No child (oras) or writer survives the tool call.
- Ordinary cancellation preserves every verified chunk/validator; only a
  real ETag/If-Range validator change resets progress.
- Resume: durable state in `data/nauka/state` + selected prefixes in
  `data/nauka/partials` on the control branch, plus GHCR checkpoint artifacts
  pulled by immutable digest and re-validated chunk-by-chunk.

## Commands (list / pull / resume)
```bash
oras repo tags ghcr.io/igor-makarov/shurik-nauka | sort
oras manifest fetch ghcr.io/igor-makarov/shurik-nauka:nij-1934-39-index | jq .
oras pull ghcr.io/igor-makarov/shurik-nauka:nij-1939-n01-djv -o ./out
node tools/nauka/cli.mjs discover
node tools/nauka/cli.mjs retrieve --budget-ms 75000
node tools/nauka/cli.mjs verify
node tools/nauka/cli.mjs index
```

Run `retrieve` directly (no `timeout`/pipe): one bounded batch, ~75 s of
transfer plus bounded cleanup, then it drains writers and exits so the
supervisor can publish at the tool boundary.

## Lifecycle / shutdown protocol
- Each `retrieve` invocation is bounded (`--budget-ms` transfer + `--cleanup-ms`
  durable checkpoint) and installs SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP + watchdog shutdown.
- On timeout/signal: in-flight HTTP requests are destroyed, queued chunks are
  skipped, `.tmp` writers are swept, state is flushed atomically and the
  process exits. No child (oras) or writer survives the tool call.
- Ordinary cancellation preserves every verified chunk/validator; only a
  real ETag/If-Range validator change resets progress.
- Resume: durable state in `data/nauka/state` + selected prefixes in
  `data/nauka/partials` on the control branch, plus GHCR checkpoint artifacts
  pulled by immutable digest and re-validated chunk-by-chunk.

## Lifecycle / shutdown protocol
- Each `retrieve` invocation is bounded (`--budget-ms` transfer + `--cleanup-ms`

- On timeout/signal: in-flight HTTP requests are destroyed, queued chunks are
  skipped, `.tmp` writers are swept, state is flushed atomically and the
  process exits. No child (oras) or writer survives the tool call.
- Ordinary cancellation preserves every verified chunk/validator; only a
  real ETag/If-Range validator change resets progress.
- Each file may hold at most `floor(concurrency / fileConcurrency)` chunks in
  the shared pool, so a large fresh file cannot starve a nearly-complete one.
- Resume: durable state in `data/nauka/state` + selected prefixes in
  `data/nauka/partials` on the control branch, plus GHCR checkpoint artifacts
  pulled by immutable digest and re-validated chunk-by-chunk.

## Lifecycle / shutdown protocol
- Each `retrieve` invocation is bounded (`--budget-ms` transfer + `--cleanup-ms`
  durable checkpoint) and installs SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP + watchdog shutdown.
- On timeout/signal: in-flight HTTP requests are destroyed, queued chunks are
  skipped, `.tmp` writers are swept, state is flushed atomically and the
  process exits. No child (oras) or writer survives the tool call.
- Ordinary cancellation preserves every verified chunk/validator; only a
  real ETag/If-Range validator change resets progress.
- Each file may hold at most `floor(concurrency / fileConcurrency)` chunks in
  the shared pool, so a large fresh file cannot starve a nearly-complete one.
- Resume: durable state in `data/nauka/state` + selected prefixes in
  `data/nauka/partials` on the control branch, plus GHCR checkpoint artifacts
  pulled by immutable digest and re-validated chunk-by-chunk.
